Requirements:
- limit positive integer, reject RangeError otherwise. What about items not array? Not specified. Should probably handle array-like? We can assume items array? But robust maybe if not array? No requirement. Don't mutate. Could use items.length and index access; if not array maybe fail. Not need.

- Call async fn(item, index) exactly once per item on successful runs. Means for each item, call fn once. But if prior rejection, should we still call remaining? "No ordering requirement for callback starts, and already running callbacks may finish after rejection." This suggests we should start up to limit, and if rejection, reject immediately? But already running callbacks may finish after rejection. Do we continue starting new callbacks after rejection? Usually mapLimit should stop starting new after error? The phrase "No ordering requirement for callback starts, and already running callbacks may finish after rejection" likely from tests: once rejected, no need to wait for running, but maybe not start new? It says "Reject if any callback throws or rejects, preserving its rejection reason. No ordering requirement for callback starts, and already running callbacks may finish after rejection." Could mean don't wait for all; reject as soon as one rejects, but already running may finish after rejection. Should we continue processing remaining? Not clear. "Call async fn(item, index) exactly once per item on successful runs" maybe if error, not necessarily successful. Standard mapLimit should stop starting new after error, reject. But "No ordering requirement for callback starts" maybe because concurrency scheduling. "already running callbacks may finish after rejection" means don't cancel promises.

Need at most limit pending invocations at any time. "pending invocations" means started promises not settled? At most limit concurrent. When one finishes, start next if no error? If error, maybe stop.

Need resolve to results in original input order regardless of completion order. So maintain order. Use results array of promises? Approach: create array of promises that map each item to promise from fn. But concurrency limit. Could implement worker pool.
